input: Write a due diligence memo on Canva

team.claim: As reported 2026-05-05, the founders were Melanie Perkins, CEO; Cliff Obrecht, COO; and Cameron Adams, chief product officer. Perkins also signed the November 2026 restructuring announcement as co-founder and CEO.
Kelly Steckelberg was hired as CFO on 2024-11-18. Previously Zoom CFO, she helped take Zoom public; earlier roles included finance positions at Cisco and CEO of Zoosk.
An interview published 2025-08-27 identifies Kelly Steckelberg as Canva CFO; a complete executive roster current to 2026-11-09 was not verified.

Canva confirmed in May 2026 that CTO Brendan Humphreys would leave in June after 12 years, remaining an adviser. Simon Newton would become head of technology rather than directly replace the CTO; Newton previously worked at Google and Uber.

funding.claim: Company announcement: raised US$200 million on 2021-09-15 at a US$40 billion valuation, led by T. Rowe Price. Participants included Franklin Templeton, Sequoia Capital Global Equities, Bessemer, Greenoaks, Dragoneer, Blackbird, Felicis and AirTree.

Reuters reported an employee share sale launched 2025-08-20 at a US$42 billion valuation, led by existing shareholder Fidelity Management, with J.P. Morgan Asset Management joining. This was secondary employee liquidity, not evidence of equivalent new capital for Canva; sale proceeds were not disclosed in the opened text.

Latest dated valuation report verified, 2026-09-18: Forbes Australia reported implied investor marks of US$38.2 billion at T. Rowe Price, US$39.3 billion at Franklin Templeton and US$34.9 billion at Blackbird. These are differing holding valuations, not a new financing price; the Franklin mark was for the quarter ended 2026-06-30.

output.verdict: Canva has substantial company-reported paid adoption, a large recurring-revenue base and credible enterprise distribution. However, the November 2026 restructuring, lower growth guidance and investor markdowns make AI unit economics, retention, organizational execution and valuation the immediate diligence priorities. Proceed to deeper diligence rather than anchor underwriting to the historical US$42 billion secondary price.

business.claim: Sydney-based visual communication software platform offering templates and drag-and-drop creation; its suite has expanded into spreadsheets and project management. Customers range from individual creators and classrooms to businesses.
Company claim: freemium model gives users a free core product and monetizes premium content, collaboration and AI tools. As of 2025-11-04, this model supported more than 28 million paying customers.
Company claim: enterprise offering adds brand governance, collaboration and security for large organizations; distribution includes integrations and reseller/consulting partners.
North America remained its largest market as reported 2026-02-18; Canva was introducing lower-priced subscriptions in Pakistan, Uruguay, Morocco and Jamaica.

traction.claim: Company claim, reported by TechCrunch: Canva ended 2025 with more than 265 million monthly active users and more than 31 million paid users.
Company claim: as reported 2025-12-15, 100 million teachers, students and education leaders used Canva monthly across more than 190 countries.

Company claim as of 2025-06-11: thousands of companies used Canva Enterprise; named customers included FedEx, Salesforce, Expedia, Reddit, DocuSign and Zoom. The separate claim that 95% of Fortune 500 companies use Canva does not establish enterprise-wide paid deployment.
Company claim as of 2025-06-11: FedEx deployed Canva across 1,400 teams in 45 countries and reduced brand-review time by 77%; these are company case-study outcomes, not independently audited results.
Company claim as of 2025-06-11: integrations included LinkedIn and HubSpot; reseller and partner relationships included SoftBank, CDW, Designit and Deloitte.
Company claim reported 2026-02-18: B2B business, defined as customers with more than 25 seats, doubled to $500 million ARR at end-2025.

red_flags.claim: Execution and organizational risk: the company acknowledged slowing growth and changes affecting 22% of staff as of 2026-11-03; impact is broader than layoffs alone.
AI economics and valuation risk: lower 2026 growth guidance, cost-related product delays and divergent investor markdowns weaken reliance on the 2025 US$42 billion secondary valuation.
Technology-leadership continuity merits diligence: the CTO departure announced in May 2026 coincided with a substantial AI transition.
Security diligence remains material given the historical mass-account breach and later disclosure of decrypted passwords; these events do not themselves establish a current vulnerability.
Employee sentiment warrants monitoring: anonymous November 2026 review trends show declining culture and work-life-balance scores, subject to selection bias.

reputation.claim: Anonymous-review aggregator Glassdoor, November 2026 snapshot accessed as of 2026-11-09: overall rating 3.8/5 and 71% recommendation. Its trend summaries show culture/values down 2% and work-life balance down 7% over the preceding year. Self-selected reviews are directional, not representative workforce measures; review totals vary within the page.

Customer-review aggregator Trustpilot, snapshot accessed as of 2026-11-09: 4.0/5 from 8,296 reviews. Its AI-generated review summary praises ease of use and templates, while identifying complaints about slow support, difficulty reaching live agents and premium-feature restrictions. These are reviewer reports, not independently established service-failure rates.

Following backlash over Teams price increases, Canva said on 2024-10-09 it would retain original pricing for early Teams users and introduce a pricing promise, including at least 60 days notice of changes. This historical episode indicates pricing sensitivity, not an unresolved universal increase.

missing_fields: Full executive roster verified as of 2026-11-09; current CFO confirmation newer than August 2025; founders prior-company histories from opened pages
Names and effective dates of other senior departures during 2024-11-09 to 2026-11-09
Complete historical funding ledger, cumulative primary capital raised, exact 2025 secondary proceeds, and any verified 2026 primary round
Audited financial statements; recognized revenue reconciliation; gross margins; AI inference costs; profitability; operating cash flow; debt and current cash balance
Exact post-restructuring headcount and redundancy count; current hiring plan
Retention, churn, customer concentration, CAC, LTV, ARPU and precise paid Enterprise customer count
Regulator decisions or enforcement outcomes; comprehensive current litigation status and original court orders; copyright/AI-training exposure
Independent security assessment and verified incident history after 2019
Sanctions/beneficial-ownership screening and geographic revenue exposure; no sanctions clearance established
Representative employee-turnover data and quantified customer complaint or refund rates
Current plan prices: pricing page returned an unsupported-client notice

financial_signals.claim: Company claim in its 2025 review, published 2025-12-15: reached US$3.5 billion in revenue. The statement does not provide audited accounts or sufficient detail to establish recognized calendar-year revenue; do not equate it with ARR.
Company figures reported by TechCrunch: end-2025 ARR was US$4 billion. ARR is a run-rate metric, not recognized annual revenue; no audited reconciliation was provided.

Forbes Australia reported on 2026-09-18 that Canva told investors in July it expected 2026 revenue growth of 20%, down from an earlier 30% forecast, alongside AI-cost concerns and delayed product rollouts.

Company claim, announcement dated 2026-11-03: organizational changes would affect 1,271 people, or 22% of Canva. Impact includes role changes, relocation and redundancies; it is not a confirmed count of layoffs alone. Product, growth and platform teams would be combined.

Company claim, 2026-11-03: growth had slowed for the first time in a decade; restructuring would centralize teams and reduce specialization. The company said teams operated across 37 countries as of the announcement.

legal_and_regulatory.claim: Company incident disclosure: the 2019-05-24 attack exposed profile data for more than 139 million users and protected password hashes for direct-login users. Canva said it found no indication that designs or images were accessed.
Company incident update: on 2020-01-11 Canva learned approximately 4 million affected passwords had been decrypted and shared online; it invalidated unchanged passwords and notified users.
CourtListener docket mirror: Accessify patent case, W.D. Texas 6:23-cv-00727, filed 2023-10-23 and terminated 2024-11-12. The opened record does not establish a merits finding or damages award.
Justia docket mirror: HyperQuery filed a patent-infringement complaint against Canva US on 2025-02-06, W.D. Texas 7:25-cv-00055. This is an allegation; final disposition was not verified.

PACERMonitor docket mirror: Cascade Systems patent case, W.D. Texas 7:25-cv-00217, was voluntarily dismissed on 2025-12-10 and ordered closed on 2025-12-11. Closure is not a determination on infringement.

CourtListener docket mirror: Canva US filed a declaratory-judgment patent action against DigiMedia Tech on 2025-09-10, N.D. Georgia 1:25-cv-05161. The opened record confirms filing, not a final resolution.
